questions.prompt: Which role asks: 'How do we keep the system running when things go wrong?'
questions.explanation: SRE = uptime, incident response, reliability targets.

questions.prompt: Who builds internal tools so developers can deploy their apps self-service?
questions.explanation: Platform Engineers build the internal tools and platforms other developers use.

questions.prompt: Building security in from the beginning, instead of checking it at the end, is the job of a…
questions.explanation: DevSecOps: test for vulnerabilities, safe libraries, licensing, sensitive data - security from the start.

questions.prompt: A staging environment is…
options: An exact copy of production used to test before release
The live system that users access
questions.explanation: Staging = exact copy of the live production system used to debug/test before releasing. (Not the Git staging area!)

questions.prompt: CAP theorem: how many of Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance can you fully optimise at once?
questions.explanation: You can only optimise two of the three dimensions; one is compromised - a trade-off decision.

questions.prompt: 'The system grows well with the number of users' describes…
questions.explanation: Good design: scalability (users), maintainability (developers), efficiency (resources), reliability (protection).
questions.source: Week 2 Tutorial 1 · 'What is a good design?'

questions.prompt: Which SDLC phase delivers the Software Design Document (SDD)?
questions.explanation: Design phase: define project architecture → deliverable is the SDD.

questions.prompt: Defining functional and non-functional requirements happens in which SDLC phase?
questions.explanation: Analysis: detailed expectations from stakeholders, functional & non-functional requirements.

questions.prompt: Health record system: migrating old patient data into the new system is part of…
questions.explanation: Deployment: deploy and test live, install/configure for users, migrate existing data.

questions.prompt: In the Waterfall model each phase must finish before the next one begins.
questions.explanation: Waterfall is linear and sequential; changes later are costly.

questions.prompt: Tax-filing software; rules are fixed by law and won't change. Best SDLC model?
questions.explanation: Stable, well-defined requirements up front → Waterfall.

questions.prompt: Insulin pump firmware: every dev phase needs a matching rigorous test phase. Best model?
questions.explanation: The V-Model pairs each development phase with a verification/testing phase - safety first.

questions.prompt: Huge banking system: build prototypes and assess risk in every loop. Best model?
questions.explanation: Spiral is risk-driven: planning, risk analysis, prototype, evaluation in each loop.

questions.prompt: Which combination describes the DevOps SDLC model?
questions.explanation: DevOps model: Agile + Iterative + Incremental, MVP with continuous improvement, automation.

questions.prompt: Which memory loses its content when the power goes off?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile short-term memory; SSD/HDD are non-volatile storage.

questions.prompt: SSD vs HDD - which statement is correct?
options: SSD has no moving parts and is faster
HDD is faster and more expensive
questions.explanation: SSD = flash chips, no moving parts, faster, pricier. HDD = spinning magnetic platters, cheaper per GB, slower.

questions.prompt: Fixing bugs from incident reports within agreed response times belongs to which SDLC phase?
questions.explanation: Maintenance: fix newly discovered bugs, improve performance, update features, adapt to new environments.

questions.prompt: E-commerce: ship browsing+checkout, then reviews, then recommendations. Best model?
questions.explanation: Each increment is a complete, working addition to what came before.

questions.prompt: Google Docs showing the same text to everyone at the same time illustrates…
questions.explanation: CAP: Consistency = same data at the same time, changes reflected everywhere.

questions.prompt: Which role chooses public/private/hybrid cloud and leads on-premise migration?
questions.explanation: Cloud Architect: overall infrastructure, cloud model, migration, compliance, vendor/cost management.

questions.prompt: Put the SDLC phases in order.
questions.explanation: Planning → Analysis → Design → Coding → Testing → Deployment → Maintenance, then the cycle continues.
